Converting 10 Fluid Ounces of Cooking Oil to Milliliters

Cooking oils — including vegetable, canola, olive, and avocado oil — are all measured by fluid volume in recipes, not by weight. Converting 10 fluid ounces of oil to milliliters uses the same standard multiplier as water: 29.57353 mL per fluid ounce, yielding exactly 295.74 mL. However, because oil is less dense than water, the actual weight of 10 fluid ounces of oil is only about 260 grams, not 295.74 grams.

The Mathematical Conversion Formula

Fluid ounce to milliliter conversion is independent of liquid density:

  • Total Milliliters (mL) = Fluid Ounces × 29.57353
  • 10 fl. oz. of oil × 29.57353 = 295.74 mL

Frequently Asked Questions

Q1: How many mL is 10 oz of cooking oil?

A1: 10 fluid ounces of cooking oil equals exactly 295.74 milliliters by volume. However, note that oil is less dense than water, so 10 fl oz of oil only weighs about 9.2 oz (roughly 260 grams) on a scale.

Q2: Is 10 oz of oil heavier or lighter than 10 oz of water?

A2: By volume, oil is lighter than water. 10 fluid ounces of water weighs about 295.74 grams, while 10 fluid ounces of vegetable oil weighs approximately 260 grams. Both occupy the same volume (295.74 mL), but oil has a lower density.

Q3: Can I substitute oil for butter using this 10 oz measurement?

A3: When substituting oil for butter in baking, use a 3/4 ratio. For every 10 oz of butter called for, use 7.5 oz of oil (about 222 mL). Always measure oil by fluid volume, not weight, for accuracy in baking.
